chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
about Adam (peace be upon him) — when he performed Hajj, with what did he shave his head?
So he said: 'Jibreel (peace be upon him) descended unto him with a precious gem (yaquta) from Paradise, and he passed it over his head, and his hair scattered off.'

key_terms.تَنَاثَرَ: tanathara — to scatter, disperse, or fall off; used for hair falling from Adam's head upon the gem's contact
key_terms.حَلَقَ: halq — the ritual shaving of the head, a required act (wajib) of Hajj and Umra, performed after the sacrifice
key_terms.يَاقُوتَة: yaquta — a precious gem from Paradise, classically translated as ruby or sapphire; here it serves as Adam's instrument for head-shaving during Hajj

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Adam shave his head during Hajj according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam al-Baqir (AS) about Prophet Adam (AS) and the act of halq (head-shaving) during Hajj, one of the required rites of the pilgrimage. The Imam narrates that the angel Jibreel descended to Adam with a precious stone — a yaquta (ruby or sapphire) — from Paradise, which miraculously caused Adam's hair to fall when passed over his head. This narrative situates the origin of Hajj rites in the primordial time of humanity's first prophet-father, emphasizing the divine and celestial nature of the pilgrimage institution.
